comment: hpft-shaper v2 lab registry. v3 adds scheme-E fields: per-vnic MAC, policy (design_e §3.1), e_params (design_e §5.4 initial values, tuned in M4). rdma_rules kept for the legacy static-cap controller path. Units: rate_bps absolute; PCC converts to 2^20-of-linerate units (line = 200 Gb/s).

rdma_flowtags.comment: per-(src,dst) PCC flowtags, probed via 0xdea 2026-07-11. The tag hashes (src function, dst function) and is stable across QP recreation, IP choice and reflash. KNOWN COLLISION: src vf1 and src vf2 produce identical tags for every dst (rows below are equal), so vf1->X and vf2->X RDMA budgets are inseparable at the RP - never schedule both concurrently. tx_agent_e keys RDMA budgets by 'src>dst' with fallback to the per-vnic flowtag.

policy.comment: design.md §3.2. VM == vnic in this lab. weight = W_i (inter-tenant); max_rate_bps = MaxRate_i (null = uncapped); class_weights = W_{i,TCP}/W_{i,RDMA}. per_sender_weights: 'dst_vnic|class|src_vnic' -> u (absent = 1). Receiver scheduler reads dst-VM params; sender tree reads src-VM params. MaxRate = 30G re-derived 2026-07-27 for the current 100G receiver downlink: C' = 97G over 4 dst VMs is 24.25G each, so the previous 20G standing default made 4x20 = 80G < 97G and the RECEIVER-DOWNLINK (incast) bottleneck of design.md §1.3 structurally unreachable - every run at that default only ever exercised the VM-cap layer. At 30G, 4x30 = 120G > 97G so the root layer binds under full load while a single VM alone is still capped below the link, keeping both guarantee classes reachable at the default.

control.comment: Scheme-E control plane addressing. telemetry: host -> its DPU's in-band ctl IP (PF1 SF on underlay-p1, rides the p1/switch data path per design_e §3.4 user note). pace_shim: sender host -> shim addr as reachable from that host's DPU (tmfifo). tree_stub_bps = static Tree_f until M5's sender tree. rate_export: receiver host -> its DPU rx_agent (tmfifo), fresh kernel-path byte counter for class attribution (2026-07-11).

e_params.comment: design.md §6 (v2 tracking-audit law, migrated 2026-07-27). RESPONSE LAW: the receiver synthesises one target per flow-set, u_f = ceil_f*(1-gamma*s_f) (§3.4), and the sender does first-order tracking in log space, R <- R*(u/R)^(k*T) (§4.2). No branches, no clamps, no skeleton switch: the v1 MIMD/AIMD/MIAD skeletons and every parameter that only existed to keep them stable (mi_alpha/beta/mi_bang, app-limited, fast-recovery/HAI, probe margins, MD anchors/floors, the RDMA budget descent slew) were deleted with the law. Fairness still lives entirely in the receiver's water-filling, not in the law. Params are wall-clock quantities (rate constants in s^-1, integrals in bits), so they do not need retuning when period_ms changes -- there is no ref_period_ms scaling any more. k=20 s^-1 is capped by target staleness (k*tau_eff <~ 0.4, tau_eff ~20ms); gamma=0.25 sets both the audit discount band (u >= 0.75*ceil) and the audit-loop damping (zeta = 0.5*sqrt(k*V/(gamma*ceil))); V = v_seconds*headroom*C = 600 Mbit is a wall-clock excess-integral: it must NOT scale with the control period, and it IS anchored on C, the downlink bottleneck capacity the receiver actually schedules against (100G here), not on the NIC port line rate -- ehat scales with C, so V must too or the audit loop's damping becomes link-rate dependent (design.md §3.3). rx_agent reads C from the uplink and recomputes V whenever the link speed changes. The 600 Mbit value itself is empirical (settled by the 2026-07-22 convergence campaign, halved from the AIMD-era 1.2 Gbit); design_theory §3 shows it lands 1% from the optimal-damping inverse V = 4*zeta^2*gamma*ehat_star/k at zeta=1/sqrt(2), which is post-hoc confirmation, not a derivation -- re-derive it if the tenant count, flow count, link rate or loop delay changes. Derivations and tuning rules: hpft-design/docs/design_theory.md.
